Elaine (Sales): Hey team — Janus asked for a performance plan + updated quote. They want streaming embeddings + text-generation at sustained spikes. Can ops run a focused run tomorrow morning?
Mike (EngSRE): Yep. What are target SLAs? p95/p99 and sustained qps?
Elaine (Sales): They care about interactive latency. Goal p95 < 120ms, p99 < 350ms for 512-token responses. Sustained baseline 800 rps, bursts to 3k for ~2m windows.
Ari (Solutions): For streaming we should test both small-batch steady-state and burst ramp. Suggest: 1) 800 rps steady @ burst concurrency 3k for 2m 2) Poisson-style arrival with hot prefixes (cache hit sim) 3) Long-tail sim with 2% 2k-token requests.
Sam (Product): Also capture throughput breakdown by model variant (fp16 vs 4-bit quant) and by routing policy. They want cost delta for quantized vs fp16 in the quote.
Aaron (Pricing): I'll need tokens/sec and estimated GPU-hours. If we keep latency SLOs, we'll likely use dedicated A100-like instances. Send perf numbers and I'll compute a draft price.
deply-bot: deploy scheduled: load-run-env will be provisioned at 08:00 UTC tomorrow.
Mike (EngSRE): Ops plan: run on dedicated pool with autoscale off, fixed pool of 6 nodes (8xA100 equiv) for steady-state, then add 12 nodes at burst. Use continuous batching config: batch_size=8, max_latency_ms=8.
Ari (Solutions): Load commands for the test (use k6-like tool):
```
./runtest --endpoint=https://api.redwood.example/stream 
  --model=redwood-stream-1 
  --rate=800 --dur=300 
  --burst-rate=3000 --burst-duration=120 
  --input-mix=90:short_prompt,8:medium_prompt,2:long_prompt 
```
Mike (EngSRE): Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 latency (token and resp), tail jitter, GPU util, token/sec, KV-cache hit ratio, and queue length. Also measure cold-start for scale-up path.
Elaine (Sales): Janus also flagged encryption/HSM questions and whether KMS impacts latency. @June can you confirm?
June (Security): KMS adds ~5-15ms on RPCs if we wrap per-request keys; recommend envelope encryption with KMS for key ops only. We'll include measurement variant: with KMS key fetchs cached on node and with per-request key fetch to show delta.
Ari (Solutions): Good call. We'll include two runs: KMS-cached and KMS-per-request. Add a run with prefix cache warmed and one cold.
Mike (EngSRE): I'll run three test permutations: fp16/KMS-cached/warm-cache, 4-bit/KMS-cached/warm, fp16/KMS-per-request/cold. Expect p99 delta ~+40-70ms when per-request KMS is on.
Aaron (Pricing): After runs, send me: sustained token/sec, GPU-hours used, average batch size. I'll produce 3 quote tiers (hosted, reserved, dedicated) and delta for quantized model.
Elaine (Sales): Timeline: run tomorrow 08:00 UTC, raw results by 14:00 UTC, pricing + slide by EOD. Janus wants a short summary for their engineering call on Friday.
Sam (Product): We should also capture examples where fallback routing kicks in (lower-capacity cheaper variant) to show graceful degradation. Include in the run: a simulated AZ outage where 50% capacity lost for 90s.
Mike (EngSRE): Noted. I'll script an outage step in the runbook. Will ping here when env is live.
Elaine (Sales): Thanks. @Aaron I'll DM prod volume estimates for Janus so you can tune the tiers.
Aaron (Pricing): Got it. I'll start a draft and link it once I have numbers.
deploy-bot: environment aready: load-run-env (id: lr-janus-6501) ready at 07:50 UTC.
Mike (EngSRE): Kicking off a smoke at 07:55 to sanity-check. Will report back after steady-state completes (expected ~09:05).
Elaine (Sales): Appreciate the quick turnaround. I'll update Janus and hold their call window for Friday. :thumbsup:
